summary: Stage C — patient_provider_relationships verification. Wrote 13 focused backend tests covering: (1) registration→applicant row w/ history; (2) duplicate-email 400 preserved; (3) FORMER_CLOSED match returns application_required with NO account + NO relationship (regression gate); (4) /applications/new-patient→applicant keyed by application_id; (5) physician accept transitions SAME relationship row applicant→active, anchored to exactly ONE newly-created canonical directory + patient_id + PIN with full history; (6) verify→active, reject→inactive; (7) /patients/{id}/link-directory preserves PIN, re-anchors to directory_id, creates no 2nd canonical row, returns 409 when directory already linked to a different account; (8) duplicate prevention — 3× verify ⇒ ONE relationship, history preserved; (9) GET /internal/patients/{id}/relationship returns scoped data, 404 on cross-practice; (10) GET /internal/canonical/{dir}/relationships returns full own + Practice-B status-only summary (no PHI leak); (11) /internal/identity-links scoping — Practice-B rows do NOT leak into dr-aguayo queue. Also smoke-tested Verifications UI: 10 pending items each render data-testid=relationship-own; no console errors; Identity Link Review tab currently empty in preview but renders cleanly. 13/13 backend pass, UI OK. All synthetic artefacts (TEST_STAGEC tag) cleaned up in teardown — real dr-aguayo practice, real users, demo patients, and existing 61 relationships untouched.

minor.issue: Running the Stage C suite with default pytest-xdist (-n auto, LoadScope) occasionally wiped seeded relationships mid-session when another worker's session-scoped autouse teardown fired early. Resolved by scoping teardown deletes to _test_tag=TEST_STAGEC only (no broad 'source: test_seed' delete). Not a product bug — test-infra note for next agent: run `pytest backend/tests/test_stage_c_relationships.py -o addopts='-p no:xdist'` for deterministic runs.

critical_code_review_comments: upsert_relationship de-dup priority (directory_id > patient_id > application_id) correctly merges the applicant-by-application row into the active-by-directory row on accept, with history preserved — verified empirically.

verify_patient has a slight redundancy: the 'verified + linked' branch at ~3993 and the generic fallback at ~4015 both call upsert_relationship with status=ACTIVE for the same patient. Idempotent (status unchanged on 2nd call), but one call is enough. Low-priority cleanup — consider short-circuiting the fallback when the linked branch already ran.

FORMER_CLOSED regression correctly handled: /auth/register returns application_required and NO relationship row is written on this path (verified). Good — matches the stated invariant that former status is reference-only.

Cross-practice canonical endpoint strictly returns {practice_name,status,label,practice_id,updated_at} for 'others' — no patient_id/email/name/dob/phone/PIN/HCN leak. PHI-safety verified by explicit disallow-list assertion.

server.py now ~6324 lines — compounded from the ~6181 last iteration. Stage C added ~140 lines around register/verify/link/new-patient-accept and 2 new endpoints + helpers. Factor the relationship-upsert call sites into a thinner adapter and split into server_relationships.py submodule to stay maintainable.
Stage B counters pscope fix from iteration_62 is NOT re-verified here (out of scope); keep that on the retest list.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — Verifications UI loads cleanly, 10 pending items render 10 relationship-own badges, no console errors
